explanation:
[EFFECT] Demand follows a strong double-peak pattern across the day. Contributions are most negative in the very early morning (around 4 a.m., SHAP ≈ −3.5), meaning very few rentals are predicted then. They rise sharply to a morning-rush peak around 8 a.m. (~+0.9), dip slightly mid-morning, climb again to the highest point of the day around 5 p.m. (~+1.0), and then fall steadily back through the evening.
[IMPORTANCE] This is by far the single most important feature (importance 0.833), dwarfing all others; the hour of day alone drives the largest swings in predicted demand.
[RECOMMENDATION] Staffing and bike-redistribution plans should be built primarily around the hour of the day — particularly the sharp morning (≈8 a.m.) and evening (≈5 p.m.) peaks — and adjusted for temperature, since warm mild days can roughly double predicted rentals compared with cold or very hot ones. All other factors, including weather and weekday type, provide useful fine-tuning but are secondary to getting the time-of-day and temperature conditions right.
